identification.summary: Microsoft describes Smoke Sandstorm as an Iranian nation-state actor, formerly tracked as BOHRIUM and DEV-0056. In September 2021 it compromised email accounts at a Bahrain-based IT integration company whose Bahrain Government clients were likely the ultimate target [S1]. Microsoft maps Mandiant's UNC1549 and CrowdStrike's IMPERIAL KITTEN to Smoke Sandstorm [S8]. Google Threat Intelligence (Mandiant) describes UNC1549 as an Iran-nexus espionage group targeting aerospace, aviation and defense organizations and their third-party suppliers [S3][S4]. Check Point tracks the overlapping cluster as Nimbus Manticore and reported a new backdoor, MiniFast, in 2026 [S7].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft: earliest dated activity September 2021 [S1]. Mandiant: UNC1549 active since at least June 2022 [S3]. CrowdStrike: IMPERIAL KITTEN active since at least 2017 (reported by The Hacker News) [S6].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Smoke Sandstorm (formerly BOHRIUM, DEV-0056) [S1]. Microsoft's mapping lists IMPERIAL KITTEN and UNC1549 under Smoke Sandstorm [S8]. MITRE tracks NIMBUS MANTICORE as G1059 and lists UNC1549 and TA455 as associated names [S9]. The Hacker News lists GalaxyGato, Nimbus Manticore and Subtle Snail as other names for UNC1549 [S5]. Mandiant's 2024 report noted overlaps with both Tortoiseshell and Smoke Sandstorm/BOHRIUM [S3]. Cluster scopes differ by vendor; see gaps.

attribution.sponsor: Iran. Microsoft lists Iran as the country of origin [S1]. CrowdStrike assesses that IMPERIAL KITTEN likely fulfills Iranian strategic intelligence requirements associated with IRGC operations (as reported by The Hacker News) [S6]. Check Point and press coverage describe Nimbus Manticore as IRGC-affiliated [S7].
attribution.confidence: Mandiant assessed the Iran nexus of UNC1549 with moderate confidence, citing overlaps with Tortoiseshell, which has been linked to the IRGC [S3]. The 2025 GTIG report calls UNC1549 a suspected Iran-nexus, Iranian-backed group and does not name the IRGC [S4]. The IRGC link rests on vendor assessments; no government attribution was found in the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry and its 2022 civil legal action against BOHRIUM infrastructure [S1][S2]; Mandiant/GTIG incident response [S3][S4]; CrowdStrike and Check Point reporting, relayed by press coverage [S6][S7].

objectives: Espionage. GTIG says UNC1549 primarily seeks network and IT documentation, intellectual property and email, and uses compromised organizations as pivots into their industry partners [S4]. Microsoft assesses that its Middle East targeting serves sectors of interest to the Iranian regime, including government, defense and transportation [S1].

sectors: Defense contractors and their third-party suppliers [S4]
Government (Bahrain Government via an IT integrator) [S1]
regions: Middle East: Bahrain [S1]; Israel and UAE [S3]
Europe and the United States (2026 Check Point reporting) [S7]
targeting.notes: Microsoft's BOHRIUM reporting stresses supply-chain-style access through IT integrators [S1]. GTIG emphasizes abuse of trusted third parties to reach defense primes [S4]. CrowdStrike's IMPERIAL KITTEN reporting focuses on Israeli transportation, logistics and technology firms [S6].

capabilities.summary: Social engineering with fake recruiter personas and job lures, used by BOHRIUM in 2022 and by UNC1549 through 2025 [S2][S3][S4]. Initial access through trusted third-party relationships and VDI breakouts from Citrix, VMware and Azure Virtual Desktop environments provided to partners [S4]. Custom backdoors and tunnelers: MINIBIKE and MINIBUS [S3]; TWOSTROKE, DEEPROOT, POLLBLEND, GHOSTLINE and LIGHTRAIL [S4]; MiniFast (2026) [S7]. Credential theft through DCSync (DCSYNCER.SLICK), Kerberoasting, AD CS abuse, browser-credential theft (CRASHPAD) and a fake Outlook prompt (TRUSTTRAP) [S4]. Heavy use of Microsoft Azure infrastructure for C2, including more than 125 Azure subdomains in 2024, and lookalike aerospace career domains [S3][S4]. Defense evasion through DLL search-order hijacking of legitimate vendor binaries, unique per-payload hashes, legitimately signed backdoors, reverse SSH tunnels and dormant backdoors that reactivate after eradication [S4]. CrowdStrike reports watering holes, VPN credential theft, one-day exploitation and IMAPLoader malware under IMPERIAL KITTEN [S6]. Check Point assesses that MiniFast code appears AI-assisted [S7].

campaigns.name: Bahrain IT integrator compromise
campaigns.summary: Compromised email accounts at a Bahrain-based IT integrator serving Bahrain Government clients, plus accounts at a partly government-owned Middle East ICT provider serving defense and transportation.

campaigns.name: Microsoft DCU disruption of BOHRIUM
campaigns.summary: Microsoft obtained a court order and seized 41 domains used in BOHRIUM recruiter-themed spear-phishing against tech, transport, government and education targets in the US, Middle East and India.

campaigns.name: IMPERIAL KITTEN targeting of Israeli transport and logistics
campaigns.summary: CrowdStrike reported intrusions into Israeli transportation, logistics and technology organizations, plus a multiyear watering-hole effort.

campaigns.name: UNC1549 Middle East aerospace and defense campaign
campaigns.summary: Mandiant reported job and Israel-Hamas-themed lures delivering MINIBIKE and MINIBUS via Azure C2 against aerospace and defense targets in Israel, UAE and nearby states.

campaigns.name: UNC1549 third-party and VDI intrusions
campaigns.summary: GTIG detailed intrusions since mid-2024 against aerospace, aviation and defense using supplier pivots, VDI breakouts, TWOSTROKE and DEEPROOT.

campaigns.name: Nimbus Manticore MiniFast campaign
campaigns.summary: Check Point reported aviation- and software-themed lures across the US, Europe and the Middle East delivering the MiniFast backdoor.

diamond.adversary: Iranian state-linked operators that Microsoft tracks as Smoke Sandstorm [S1]. Vendors link the overlapping clusters to the IRGC at varying confidence [S3][S6][S7].
diamond.capability: Recruiter and job lures; MINIBIKE/MINIBUS, TWOSTROKE, DEEPROOT, LIGHTRAIL and MiniFast; DCSync, Kerberoasting, AD CS abuse and RDP hijacking [S3][S4][S7].
diamond.infrastructure: Azure-hosted C2 (azurewebsites.net, cloudapp.azure.com), lookalike career domains, reverse SSH tunnel endpoints, ZeroTier and ngrok [S3][S4]. In 2022 Microsoft seized 41 BOHRIUM domains [S2].
diamond.victim: Aerospace, aviation and defense firms and their suppliers; government clients reached through IT integrators; transportation and technology firms in the Middle East, Europe, the US and India [S1][S2][S3][S4][S7].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection on defense and aerospace programs and on regional governments, aligned with Iranian regime interests [S1][S4]. Lures exploited the Israel-Hamas conflict [S3].
diamond.technology: Trust relationships between primes and suppliers, partner-facing VDI (Citrix, VMware, AVD), Active Directory and Azure AD Connect, and cloud hosting that blends with legitimate Azure traffic [S3][S4].

gaps: Cluster boundaries: Microsoft maps IMPERIAL KITTEN to Smoke Sandstorm [S8], but CrowdStrike's IMPERIAL KITTEN reporting (IMAPLoader, watering holes, since 2017) overlaps with Tortoiseshell-associated activity, and Mandiant noted overlaps with both Tortoiseshell and Smoke Sandstorm [S3][S6]. Do not merge IMPERIAL KITTEN facts into Smoke Sandstorm without vendor confirmation.
MITRE G1059 (NIMBUS MANTICORE) also lists Proofpoint's TA455; Microsoft's mapping does not name TA455 under Smoke Sandstorm. The encyclopedia keeps TA455 as a separate record [S8][S9].

Check Point's 2025 report on Nimbus Manticore expanding into Europe (MiniJunk, MiniBrowse) was referenced in searches but could not be opened (host unreachable), and its date was not confirmed. It is not cited.

Secondary coverage says Check Point observed three Nimbus Manticore waves from February to April 2026, coinciding with the US 'Operation Epic Fury', and a first use of SEO poisoning that impersonated Oracle SQL Developer. Sources for this were undated aggregator pages and were not verified against the primary report.
Kaspersky reporting (NodeRabbit, PollCat, fake coding tests) and Nextron reporting (a fake Ebix recruiter) on Nimbus Manticore surfaced only in search snippets and were not verified.
Dark Reading reported 2025 targeting expansion to the US, UAE, Qatar, Spain and Saudi Arabia; the article date was not confirmed, so it is not cited.
Primary documents not opened: Microsoft's 2022 BOHRIUM blog and civil action filing, CrowdStrike's IMPERIAL KITTEN report, and Check Point's research posts.
No government (USG) attribution or advisory specific to Smoke Sandstorm was found in the sources gathered.
Unit 42 reportedly found no confirmed breaches of targeted oil, gas or aviation firms in the 2026 activity (secondary snippet only, unverified).

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (operational environment): Key terrain includes defense-industrial-base suppliers, IT integrators and partner-facing VDI (Citrix, VMware, AVD) that bridge into prime contractors and government clients, as well as Active Directory and Azure AD Connect [S1][S4]. STEP 2 (effects): Supplier and integrator compromises let the actor bypass hardened primes, and Azure-hosted C2 blends with legitimate cloud traffic [S3][S4]. STEP 3 (adversary model): Recruiter or job lure, or a supplier pivot, then a custom backdoor (MINIBUS, TWOSTROKE, DEEPROOT, MiniFast), then DCSync and Kerberoasting, then RDP lateral movement, then collection of IT documentation, IP and email [S3][S4][S7]. STEP 4 (COAs): MLCOA is persistent espionage against aerospace, aviation and defense suppliers supporting US and partner programs, timed with regional conflict [S4][S7]. MDCOA is the use of supplier access and domain-controller credential resets to cause outages or set up follow-on disruption during an Iran-related crisis; GTIG notes that DC account password resets have already caused outages [S4]. Candidate indicators: job-themed archives from lookalike career domains; DLL side-loading of signed Fortinet, VMware, Citrix or NVIDIA binaries from unusual paths; new reverse SSH tunnels, ZeroTier or ngrok after remediation; DCSync from non-DC hosts; unexpected azurewebsites.net or cloudapp.azure.com beacons [S3][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: fuse DIB supplier compromise reporting with DoD network telemetry, because the actor reaches targets through third parties and partner VDI [S4]. (2) Authorities: much of the relevant terrain sits in contractor and cloud-provider space, so response depends on DC3 and the DIB CS program, cloud-provider takedowns (Microsoft's 2022 domain seizure is a precedent) and law-enforcement partners rather than DoD actions alone [S2][S4]. (3) Mission assurance: dormant backdoors reactivate after eradication, so restoration plans must include full credential and trust resets (including AD CS and Azure AD Connect) and post-remediation hunts [S4]. (4) Coordination: activity has tracked Middle East conflict cycles, so share indicators with coalition partners in Israel, the Gulf and Europe during escalation periods [S3][S7].
